Google Analytics 4 and Search Console set up

Netlify deployment, 1 language, 2 defined revision rounds

pageCount.label: How many core pages does your website need?

languageCount.label: How many languages does the website need?

needsEcommerce.label: Do you need an online shop with payment processing?

needsBookingOrCrm.label: Do you need a booking flow or a CRM connection?

needsCustomApps.label: Do you need custom applications, a member area, API integrations, or AI workflows?

hasOwnCopy.label: Do you already have your page copy ready (or is copywriting planned separately)?
hasOwnCopy.helpText: Does not change the recommended tier, but is reflected in the result as a reminder, since copywriting is not included in the Starter package.

decisionLogic.description: A deterministic rule set that maps the reader's own answers onto the three real packages defined in pricing.ts. No weighting, no score, no random factor - every recommendation must be traceable back to the specific answers that produced it.

rules.condition: needsEcommerce === true OR needsCustomApps === true OR pageCount === '20+'
rules.reason: E-commerce, custom applications/API integrations/AI workflows, and more than 20 pages fall outside both Starter and Business and belong structurally to the Complex/Custom Website from CHF 9,900, regardless of the other answers.

rules.condition: pageCount === '6-20' OR languageCount === '2+' OR needsBookingOrCrm === true
rules.reason: More than 5 pages, multiple languages, or a booking/CRM connection are explicit Business Website characteristics per pricing.ts (10-20 pages, multilingual-ready, booking/CRM connection where applicable) and are not part of the Starter scope.

rules.condition: pageCount === '1-5' AND languageCount === '1' AND needsEcommerce === false AND needsBookingOrCrm === false AND needsCustomApps === false
rules.reason: The requirement fits entirely inside the approved Starter scope: up to 5 pages, 1 language, no e-commerce, no booking/CRM connection, no custom applications.

decisionLogic.note: Rules are checked in the order listed; the first matching rule determines the result. If no rule matches (should not occur for complete answers), no result is shown - instead a note that the combination should be discussed in a free consultation.

boundaryGuidance.description: An honest note for borderline cases, so the tool never quietly nudges the reader toward the more expensive option.
boundaryGuidance.text: If your page count is only just above 5 (say, 6 or 7) and that extra page is the only reason the tool suggested Business, it may be cheaper to condense your content into 5 core pages and stay with the Starter package instead of moving into the Business category. The tool shows this note precisely when pageCount = '6-20' was the sole condition that triggered the Business recommendation.

copyReminder: When hasOwnCopy = false (or left unanswered), show this note regardless of the recommended package: 'Copywriting is not included in the Starter package; check for every category whether copywriting needs to be planned as a separate item.'
disclaimer: This recommendation is based solely on your own answers and on Weissmann AI's publicly listed package definitions (as of 29 July 2026, see weissmann.ai/en/preise/). It is a non-binding indication, not a quote or a contract. The actual scope and price are only fixed during a consultation or at checkout. All calculations run locally in your browser; no data is transmitted or stored.

starter.label: See current prices and the Starter package

business.label: Free consultation about the Business Website

complex.label: Free consultation about the Complex/Custom Website

comparisonView.description: A secondary, always-visible mode alongside the fit-checker questionnaire: a plain side-by-side visual comparison of all three real tiers (price, page range, languages, revision rounds, and the three headline features each), so a reader who does not want to answer six questions can still see the honest shape of all three packages at a glance before deciding whether to use the questionnaire at all.
comparisonView.highlightRule: Never pre-select or visually emphasize one column as 'recommended' before the reader has answered the questionnaire - all three columns are shown with equal visual weight in comparison mode.
